title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A cryptocurrency trading scam exploited a retired couple by combining social engineering with a fake website that displayed fabricated account balances. A stranger initiated contact through WhatsApp and directed the victim to a mobile trading app, then used a fake AI-generated website to show false transaction history and withdrawals, creating the illusion of legitimate returns on growing investments. The scammers maintained trust through small successful withdrawals before the victim attempted a larger one that exposed the fraud.

This is a deployment failure in the interface between the victim and the financial system. The fake website presented false data as fact without any verification step, and the scammers exploited the absence of authentication between the app and what the user saw on screen. The scheme would have been caught by a system that required independent confirmation of account status through official channels or that verified the origin and encryption of account information before display.

Not established: whether the trading app itself had security flaws, whether the AI generation of the website was material to the deception, or whether recovery efforts succeeded.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that began when a stranger contacted them through WhatsApp. The scammer encouraged Jerry Dunaway to invest using a mobile trading app and gained his trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts. Over time, Jerry increased his investments, believing he was seeing legitimate returns on his account.

The couple discovered the fraud when Jerry tried to make a larger withdrawal and was unable to access the funds. Police determined that while the trading app itself was real, scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that displayed false account information on Jerry's screen. The couple is now working with Gwinnett County police, though investigators indicate victims in similar cases rarely recover their money. Their children have started a GoFundMe page to help the Dunaways with expenses as they work to rebuild their lives.
